lessons.title: Such was the demand that...
lessons.title_uz: Fronting: Such was..., So great was..., Strange as it may seem
lessons.goal_uz: Gapning muhim qismini boshiga chiqarib (fronting), ta'kid va kontrastni kuchaytirasiz: Such was the demand that..., Much as I admire..., Try as I might... — badiiy va publitsistik uslub uchun.

words.ex: The response from readers was overwhelming.

steps.title: The novel nobody wanted
steps.text: Such was the demand for Malika Karimova's debut novel that the first print run sold out within a week. Few had expected it. Rejected by eleven publishers, the manuscript had spent three years in a drawer. "Try as I might, I couldn't find anyone who believed in it," she recalls. So overwhelming was the response from readers, however, that the book has now been translated into six languages and has won international acclaim. Much as critics admire her style, some have reservations about the ending, which they describe as rushed. Karimova is unconcerned. "Strange as it may seem, I never wrote for critics. I wrote for my grandmother, who never learned to read." Whatever the critics say, her resilience is a lesson to every young writer who has searched in vain for a publisher.
steps.uz: Malika Karimovaning birinchi romaniga talab shunchalik katta ediki, birinchi adadi bir hafta ichida sotilib ketdi. Buni kam odam kutgan edi. O'n bitta nashriyot rad etgan qo'lyozma uch yil tortmada yotgan edi. "Qanchalik urinmay, unga ishonadigan odam topolmadim", — deb eslaydi u. Biroq o'quvchilarning munosabati shunchalik kuchli bo'ldiki, kitob hozir oltita tilga tarjima qilingan va xalqaro e'tirofga sazovor bo'lgan. Tanqidchilar uning uslubiga qanchalik qoyil qolmasin, ba'zilari yakuniga nisbatan e'tirozlarini bildirib, uni shoshilinch yozilgan deb ta'riflaydi. Karimova esa xotirjam. "G'alati tuyulishi mumkin, lekin men hech qachon tanqidchilar uchun yozmaganman. Men o'qishni o'rganmagan buvim uchun yozganman." Tanqidchilar nima demasin, uning chidamliligi nashriyot izlab behuda yurgan har bir yosh yozuvchi uchun saboqdir.

steps.title_uz: Fronting — muhim qismni gap boshiga chiqarish
steps.body_uz:
C2 darajasida ta'kid uchun gapning bir qismini **boshiga chiqaramiz**. Bu badiiy matn, nutq va publitsistikada juda ko'p uchraydi.
**1) Such + be + ot + that** (= shunchalik katta ediki): The demand was so great that... → **Such was the demand that** the book sold out.
**2) So + sifat + be + ega + that**: The response was so overwhelming that... → **So overwhelming was the response that**...
**3) Sifat / ravish + as + ega + fe'l** (= although, qanchalik ... bo'lmasin): Although it may seem strange → **Strange as it may seem**, ... · **Tired as she was**, she kept working.
**4) Much as + ega + fe'l** (= although ... very much): **Much as I admire** him, I can't agree.
**5) Try as + ega + might** (= qanchalik urinmasin): **Try as I might**, I couldn't open it.
Tayyor iboralar: **Come what may** (nima bo'lsa ham) · **Be that as it may** (shunday bo'lsa ham).
⚠️ "Such was **a** demand" — xato (artikl yo'q). "So **the response was** overwhelming that" — xato: so + sifat + **be + ega**.

steps.prompt_uz: Siz bilgan biror insonning (yoki o'zingizning) qiyinchilikni yengib, muvaffaqiyatga erishgani haqida qisqa hikoya yozing (100+ so'z). Kamida uchta fronting tuzilmasi ishlating: Such was..., So ... was..., Much as..., Try as ... might, ... as it may seem.
steps.prompt: Write a short story about someone who overcame a difficulty and succeeded. Use at least three fronted structures (Such was..., So ... was..., Much as..., Try as ... might, Strange as it may seem).
steps.example: When my cousin Bekzod decided to become a programmer at the age of thirty-five, most of our family laughed. Much as they loved him, they thought he was far too old to start again. Try as he might, he could not find a course that fitted around his job at the bazaar, so he taught himself at night using free online lessons. Such was his determination that he practised for three hours every evening, even during Ramadan. The first year was exhausting, and so many were his failed applications that he almost gave up. Strange as it may seem, it was a rejection email with detailed feedback that changed everything. Six months later, he was hired by a start-up in Tashkent, and he now leads a small team of developers.

lessons.title: It would appear that...
lessons.goal_uz: Da'voning kuchini aniq o'lchab berasiz: isbotlanganini kuchaytirasiz (undeniably, there is little doubt), taxminni yumshatasiz (it would appear, may well) — akademik Writing va Reading'da muallif fikrini tanish uchun.

words.ex: The trip was ostensibly for business.
Presumably, the meeting has been cancelled.

steps.title: Does coffee help you live longer?
steps.text: A large new study would appear to suggest that people who drink two or three cups of coffee a day live longer than those who drink none. Undeniably, the correlation is striking, and the sample of over 400,000 adults is impressive. However, correlation does not necessarily imply causation. Coffee drinkers may well differ from non-drinkers in other important ways: they are presumably more likely to have office jobs, regular routines and higher incomes, all of which tend to be associated with better health. The authors themselves acknowledge this caveat, describing their findings as tentative. This is not to say that the results are meaningless; rather, they point to an area that merits further research. Newspaper headlines announcing that "coffee makes you live longer", by contrast, go far beyond what the evidence can substantiate.
steps.uz: Yangi katta tadqiqot ko'rinishidan, kuniga ikki-uch chashka qahva ichadigan odamlar umuman ichmaydiganlarga qaraganda uzoqroq yashashini ko'rsatayotganga o'xshaydi. Shubhasiz, bu bog'liqlik hayratlanarli, 400 000 dan ortiq kattalardan iborat tanlanma ham ta'sirli. Biroq o'zaro bog'liqlik har doim ham sababiyatni anglatmaydi. Qahva ichuvchilar ichmaydiganlardan boshqa muhim jihatlarda ham farq qilishi mumkin: ehtimol, ular ofisda ishlashi, muntazam kun tartibiga va yuqoriroq daromadga ega bo'lishi ehtimoli ko'proq — bularning barchasi odatda yaxshi sog'liq bilan bog'liq. Mualliflarning o'zlari bu ogohlantirishni tan olib, natijalarini dastlabki deb ta'riflashadi. Bu natijalar ma'nosiz degani emas; aksincha, ular qo'shimcha tadqiqotga arziydigan sohani ko'rsatadi. "Qahva umrni uzaytiradi" degan gazeta sarlavhalari esa dalillar asoslay oladigan narsadan ancha oshib ketadi.

steps.body_uz:
C2 darajasidagi yozuvchi har bir da'voning **qanchalik ishonchli** ekanini aniq ko'rsatadi.
**Hedging (yumshatish)** — taxmin va talqinlar uchun: **It would appear / seem that...** · X **would appear to** suggest... · X **may well** be... · **tend to** · **There is some evidence to suggest that...** · **to a certain extent** · **presumably** (mantiqan taxmin qilsak).
**Boosting (kuchaytirish)** — isbotlangan faktlar uchun: **undeniably** · **clearly** · **There is little doubt that...** · **It is beyond dispute that...**
**Distancing (masofa saqlash)** — o'zingiz rozi bo'lmagan da'volar uchun: **ostensibly** (zohiran, lekin aslida...) · **allegedly** · **It is claimed that...**
**Balanslash**: **This is not to say that** X; **rather**, Y.
⚠️ Xato: hamma narsani yumshatish ("It may possibly perhaps seem...") — fikr yo'qolib qoladi. Ham xato: taxminni fakt sifatida berish ("Coffee makes you live longer.")

steps.prompt_uz: Quyidagi da'vo haqida bitta akademik paragraf yozing (120+ so'z): "Video games make children violent." Isbotlangan narsani kuchaytiring (undeniably, there is little doubt), taxminlarni yumshating (it would appear, may well) va "This is not to say that... ; rather, ..." ishlating.
steps.prompt: Write one academic paragraph evaluating the claim "Video games make children violent." Use boosting, hedging and "This is not to say that...; rather, ...".
steps.example: It is frequently claimed that violent video games turn children into aggressive adults. There is little doubt that many popular games contain disturbing images, and some studies have found a correlation between heavy gaming and short-term aggressive behaviour. However, it would appear that this link is considerably weaker than headlines suggest. Children who play violent games for many hours may well differ from their peers in other respects, such as the amount of parental supervision they receive or the stress they experience at home, and these factors could presumably explain much of the difference. Moreover, crime among young people has fallen in many countries during the same decades in which gaming has grown. This is not to say that parents should ignore what their children play; rather, the evidence suggests that games are one factor among many and are unlikely, on their own, to cause violence.

lessons.title: A double-edged sword
lessons.goal_uz: Publitsistika va inshoda ishlatsa bo'ladigan obrazli iboralarni (pave the way, a watershed moment, a drop in the ocean) o'rganasiz va metaforalarni aralashtirib yuborish xatosidan qochasiz.

words.uz: ikki tig'li qilich (ham foyda, ham zarar)
words.ex: Fame is a double-edged sword.
The discovery paved the way for new vaccines.
The industry is at a crossroads.

words.uz: dengizdan bir tomchi (kerakli miqdorga nisbatan juda oz)
words.ex: The donation was a drop in the ocean.
The election was a watershed moment for the country.
Our efforts finally bore fruit.

words.uz: sirpanchiq yo'l (kichik qadam katta muammoga olib boradi)
words.ex: Borrowing to pay debts is a slippery slope.
New laws failed to stem the tide of fake news.

steps.title: Editorial: AI in the classroom
steps.text: Artificial intelligence in education is a double-edged sword. On the one hand, it has paved the way for genuinely personalised learning: a student in a remote village can now receive instant feedback on an essay at midnight. On the other hand, critics warn that allowing students to use chatbots for homework is a slippery slope — today an essay outline, tomorrow the entire essay. Attempts to stem the tide of AI-written assignments through bans have so far proved largely futile, since students can access the technology on their phones. Schools, in short, are at a crossroads. Many educators regard this as a watershed moment, comparable to the arrival of the calculator. Yet the government's recent investment in teacher training, though welcome, is a drop in the ocean compared with what is needed. Whether the current experiments will bear fruit remains to be seen.
steps.uz: Ta'limdagi sun'iy intellekt — ikki tig'li qilich. Bir tomondan, u chinakam shaxsiylashtirilgan ta'limga yo'l ochdi: olis qishloqdagi talaba endi yarim tunda inshosiga darhol fikr-mulohaza olishi mumkin. Boshqa tomondan, tanqidchilar talabalarga uy vazifasi uchun chatbotlardan foydalanishga ruxsat berish — sirpanchiq yo'l, deb ogohlantiradi: bugun insho rejasi, ertaga butun insho. Taqiqlar orqali sun'iy intellekt yozgan topshiriqlar oqimini to'xtatishga urinishlar hozircha deyarli befoyda bo'ldi, chunki talabalar bu texnologiyadan telefonlarida foydalana oladi. Qisqasi, maktablar hal qiluvchi tanlov oldida turibdi. Ko'plab pedagoglar buni kalkulyator paydo bo'lishi bilan qiyoslasa bo'ladigan burilish nuqtasi deb hisoblaydi. Biroq hukumatning o'qituvchilarni tayyorlashga yaqinda kiritgan sarmoyasi, garchi ijobiy bo'lsa-da, kerakli miqdorga nisbatan dengizdan bir tomchi. Hozirgi tajribalar samara beradimi-yo'qmi — buni vaqt ko'rsatadi.

steps.explain_uz: "On the one hand... On the other hand..." — ham foyda, ham xavf.

steps.q: What does the writer think about the government's investment in teacher training?

steps.explain_uz: "a drop in the ocean compared with what is needed" — kerakli miqdorga nisbatan juda oz.

steps.body_uz:
C1 darajasidagi Speaking idiomalari (a piece of cake, hit the books) Writing'da norasmiy eshitiladi. Lekin **publitsistik metaforalar** gazeta tahririyati, ma'ruza va inshoda keng ishlatiladi.
**Ma'nosi va ishlatilishi:**
**a double-edged sword** — ham foyda, ham zarar · **pave the way for** + ot — yo'l ochmoq · **at a crossroads** — muhim tanlov oldida · **a drop in the ocean** — kerakliga nisbatan juda oz · **a watershed moment** — tarixiy burilish · **bear fruit** — samara bermoq (o'tgan zamon: **bore**) · **a slippery slope** — bitta kichik qadam boshqarib bo'lmas jarayonni boshlaydi · **stem the tide of** — kuchli oqimni to'xtatmoq.
**Qoidalar:** 1) Ibora shakli o'zgarmaydi, faqat fe'l zamoni o'zgaradi: paved the way, **bore** fruit. 2) Bir inshoda 2–3 tadan ko'p emas. 3) ⚠️ **Mixed metaphor** — ikkita metaforani aralashtirmang: "We must stem the tide before it bears fruit" — kulgili va mantiqsiz.

steps.text: Tourism is a double-edged sword: it creates jobs, but it can also damage the very places people come to see.
steps.uz: Ovoz chiqarib ayting

steps.prompt_uz: Gazeta tahririyati (editorial) uslubida qisqa matn yozing (120+ so'z): "Should cities ban cars from their centres?" Darsdagi kamida uchta obrazli iborani o'rinli ishlating va metaforalarni aralashtirmang.
steps.prompt: Write a short newspaper editorial: "Should cities ban cars from their centres?" Use at least three expressions from the lesson correctly, without mixing metaphors.
steps.example: Banning cars from city centres is, in many ways, a double-edged sword. Supporters point to cities such as Oslo, where restrictions on traffic have paved the way for quieter streets, cleaner air and busier cafés. Opponents, however, argue that such bans hit small businesses and elderly residents hardest, and they fear that closing one street is a slippery slope towards punishing anyone who needs to drive. Tashkent now finds itself at a crossroads. The handful of pedestrian streets created so far are welcome, but they are a drop in the ocean in a city of three million people and hundreds of thousands of cars. If the authorities are serious about stemming the tide of congestion, they must combine restrictions with reliable, affordable public transport. Only then will this policy bear fruit.
